 *****
 Order

The petitioner, who claims to be the owner of the property in R.S.No.9/01 measuring an extent of 9 kuzhies 12 Veesam on the North East corner located at Thattanchavady Revenue Village (previously Oulgaret Veli), has filed this writ petition for a direction to the second respondent to pay compensation to the petitioner for converting the private patta land into a burial ground as per the prevailing market rate of land similarly situated in the locality and in accordance with Act 30 of 2013 (The right to fair compensation and transparency in land acquisition, rehabilitation and resettlement act) or provide the petitioner with an alternative land under the same Municipality.
2. Heard Ms.K.Abhirami, learned counsel for petitioner and Mr.Djearaay, learned Government Advocate [P], appearing for the respondents.

3. The grievance of the petitioner is that the said property https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Writ Petition No.11697 of 2023 belongs to his mother by virtue of a French Notorial Sale deed dated 06.05.1963 and after the life time of his mother, the petitioner claims to be the legal heir by virtue of a decree passed in O.S.No.760 of 1988 by the Principal District Munsif at Pondicherry and thereby,
the petitioner has inherited the subject property.
According to the petitioner, the second respondent has unauthorisedly used the patta land as a burial ground.
The petitioner made several representations in this regard to the respondents seeking for compensation or provide an alternate land to the petitioner.
Since the same was not considered, the present writ petition has been filed before this Court.

4. Learned Government Advocate [P] appearing on behalf of respondents submitted that the subject property has been used as a burial ground for nearly five decades and it has also been categorised as a burial ground and it is shown as a burial ground in the re-survey map that was prepared in 1970's.

It was further submitted that the representation made by the petitioner has already been forwarded to the first respondent and the same is under consideration by the first respondent.
5. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Writ Petition No.11697 of 2023 case and without going into the merits of the case, it will suffice if a direction is given to the first respondent to consider the representation made by the petitioner on 21.04.2022 on its own merits and in accordance with law.
Based on the order/decision that is going to be taken by the first respondent, it will be left open to the petitioner to take further course of action in this case.

In the light of the above discussion, this writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the first respondent to consider the representation made by the petitioner on 21.04.2022 on its own merits and in accordance with law and a decision shall be taken within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
The petitioner is directed to make a fresh representation to the first respondent along with all relevant documents and also a copy of this order.
No costs.
